L0: \section{Replacement and functional universality}\label{sec:replacement}
L1: We now transfer the Gaussian limit to Rademacher couplings.  The comparison
L2: uses the spin autocorrelations themselves.  Its principal input is the
L3: averaged clock-score estimate of Proposition~\ref{prop:clock-scores}; the remaining
L4: point is to differentiate every survival and failure probability in the
L5: history construction.  Conditional copies of a checked path provide these
L6: derivatives while preserving the probability laws to which the score
L7: estimates apply.
L8: \begin{proposition}[Transfer to Rademacher disorder]\label{prop:universality}
L9: For the Rademacher coupling law,
L10: \[
L11:  \Law_{\mathrm{Rad}}\bigl(A_{n,J},B_{n,J}\bigr)
L12:  \weakto \Law_g\bigl(A_g,B_g\bigr)
L13: \]
L14: in
L15: $C_{\mathrm{loc}}((0,\infty))\times
L16: C_{\mathrm{loc}}((0,\infty)^2)$, where $(A_g,B_g)$ is the Gaussian limit
L17: obtained by combining Proposition~\ref{prop:gaussian-subsequence} with the
L18: identification of the entrance family in Theorem~\ref{thm:entrance-selection}.
L19: In particular the entrance family and the semigroup in this limit are the same $h_s^g$ and
L20: $S_t^g=\exp(-t c_*H_g)$ as in the Gaussian case, and the finite time scale is
L21: $T=T_n=n^{2/3}$.
L22: \end{proposition}
L23: Throughout this section a length $D$ of a path interval is in site-clock
L24: units.  All query legs have lengths in $[cT,CT]$, where $0<c<C<\infty$ are
L25: fixed by a compact set of query times.  We put $K=24$.  The small parameter
L26: $\beta>0$ and the convention $\lesssim_\beta$ are those of the preceding two
L27: sections.  Constants in an exponent $O(\beta)$ will depend on $K,c,C$, but
L28: not on the number of conditional-copy generations introduced below.
L29: 
L30: \subsection{Derivatives of tested histories}
L31: We first state the derivative estimate in the form needed for smooth tests
L32: of several traces.  Let $e=\{i,j\}$, $q_e(x)=x_i x_j$,
L33: $\bar q_e=\mu q_e$, and $\bar q=(\bar q_e)_e$.  Add $\vartheta$ to the
L34: interaction coefficient $J_{ij}/\sqrt n$ and set $u=\tanh\vartheta$.
L35: For a checked full history or prefix $\alpha$ of
L36: Definition~\ref{hist:tested-law}, define the unnormalized checked integral
L37: \begin{equation}\label{repl:tested-integral}
L38:  Z_{\alpha,e}(u)=
L39:  \mathbb E_{\alpha,e,u}\left[
L40:    v_\alpha
L41:    \prod_{I\in\mathscr S_\alpha}w_{I,e}(u)
L42:    \prod_{I\in\mathscr F_\alpha}(1-w_{I,e}(u))\right].
L43: \end{equation}
L44: Here $\mathbb E_{\alpha,e,u}$ is ordinary dynamics on the prescribed full
L45: history or prefix, with uniform or perturbed stationary initialization as
L46: specified by $\alpha$.  The set $\mathscr S_\alpha$ consists of its included
L47: survival checks, and $\mathscr F_\alpha$ is empty or consists of its specified
L48: first failure.  The nonnegative function $v_\alpha$ depends only on the
L49: designated initial, leg, and forest endpoints; it is independent of $u$ and
L50: common to every $e$.  Write $z_\alpha=Z_{\alpha,e}(0)$, which does not depend
L51: on $e$.  When $z_\alpha$ satisfies the inverse-polynomial lower bound in
L52: Definition~\ref{hist:tested-law}, normalizing this base integral gives the
L53: tested path law.  A product of such integrals always uses independent histories;
L54: the external tests factor separately across them.
L55: For a vector indexed by $e$, the norms $|\cdot|_p$ use uniform probability
L56: on the $\binom n2$ edges, as in Proposition~\ref{prop:clock-scores}.  Coefficients
L57: $[u^j]$ below are at $u=0$.  The distinction between coefficients and
L58: derivatives costs constants depending only on $K$.
L59: \begin{lemma}[Averaged derivatives of histories]\label{repl:history-derivatives}
L60: There are constants $a>0$ and $C_K<\infty$ with the following property for
L61: all sufficiently small fixed $\beta>0$.  Fix $A,B<\infty$, at most $K$
L62: histories of the form \eqref{repl:tested-integral}, and integers
L63: $j_\alpha\ge0$ with $1\le k=\sum_\alpha j_\alpha\le K$.  Suppose
L64: $0\le v_\alpha\le n^B$.  On the deterministic static support of
L65: Lemma~\ref{hist:static-support}, put
L66: \[
L67:  \mathscr D_e=\prod_\alpha [u^{j_\alpha}]Z_{\alpha,e}(u).
L68: \]
L69: Then, uniformly in the selected histories,
L70: \begin{align}
L71:  |\mathscr D|_1
L72:  &\le C\left(\prod_\alpha z_\alpha\right)
L73:  \begin{cases}
L74:  n^{-a+C_K\beta},&1\le k\le4,\\
L75:  n^{C_K\beta}T^{(k-4)/2},&5\le k\le K,
L76:  \end{cases}
L77:  +n^{-A},                                                     \label{repl:averaged-history}\\
L78:  |\mathscr D|_\infty
L79:  &\le C n^{C_K\beta}T^{k/2}\prod_\alpha z_\alpha+n^{-A}.
L80:                                                                \label{repl:sup-history}
L81: \end{align}
L82: The constant $C$ and the threshold for $n$ may depend on $A,B$ and on the
L83: fixed rectangles.  The exponent constant $C_K$ is independent of these
L84: precision parameters and of $\beta$.  The same estimates hold for specified
L85: derivatives in $\vartheta$ in place of the coefficients in $u$.  Signed tests
L86: are covered by applying the statement to their positive and negative parts.
L87: \end{lemma}
L88: \begin{proof}
L89: The additive precision in the lemma is useful for very small tested
L90: masses.  To prove it, first suppose each $z_\alpha\ge n^{-M}$ for a fixed
L91: $M$.  Normalize each integral by $z_\alpha$ and use the tested probability
L92: law.  The estimates below then have the factor $\prod_\alpha z_\alpha$.
L93: All exceptional contributions may be made smaller than $n^{-A'}$ for an
L94: arbitrary fixed $A'$ by the precision convention in
L95: Definition~\ref{hist:tested-law} and Proposition~\ref{prop:clock-scores}.  If some $z_\alpha<n^{-M}$,
L96: Lemma~\ref{hist:crude-ratios} and the polynomial path moments bound its
L97: unnormalized coefficients by $n^{C(K,B)}z_\alpha$.  Choosing $M$ after $A$
L98: discards all such terms at cost $n^{-A}$.  We shall use this reduction
L99: throughout the proof.
L100: \paragraph{Coefficients with fixed survival and failure weights.}
L101: We start with the terms in which no $w_I$ is differentiated.  Recall from
L102: Proposition~\ref{prop:clock-scores} that, for a node of length $D$,
L103: \begin{equation}\label{repl:score-table}
L104: \begin{aligned}
L105:  |R_l(D)|_\infty&\lesssim_\beta D^{l/2},&
L106:  |R_l(D)|_2&\lesssim_\beta D^{l/2-1},&
L107:  |R_l(D)|_4&\lesssim_\beta D^{l/2-1/2},\\
L108:  |R_3(D)|_1&\lesssim_\beta D^{-1/4},&
L109:  |R_l(D)|_1&\lesssim_\beta D^{(l-4)/2}\quad(l\ge4).
L110: \end{aligned}
L111: \end{equation}
L112: When $D\ge Tn^{-0.005}$, the $L^4$ bound for $R_1$, the $L^2$ bounds for
L113: $R_2,R_3$, and the $L^1$ bound for $R_4$ have additional factors
L114: $n^{-0.01},n^{-0.001},n^{-0.0007}$, respectively.  The notation in
L115: \eqref{repl:score-table} records the length, with the node and its fixed
L116: endpoints understood.
L117: For a last raw coefficient of order $l$ in a forward tested history, the
L118: compensation representations of
L119: Lemma~\ref{score:raw-projection} and Proposition~\ref{prop:clock-scores}(ii), with
L120: $\mathcal J_I\lesssim_\beta1$ by \eqref{score:action-bounds}, give the
L121: following costs on an interval of length
L122: $d$:
L123: \begin{equation}\label{repl:forward-costs}
L124: \begin{array}{c|c}
L125: \text{edge norm}&\text{cost after the compensation identity}\\ \hline
L126: L^2& n^{-1/2}d^{l/2-1/4}\\
L127: L^4& n^{-1/4}d^{l/2-3/16}\\
L128: L^1& n^{-1/2}\max(d^{1/2},d^{l/2-5/4}).
L129: \end{array}
L130: \end{equation}
L131: Each line allows a factor $n^{O(\beta)}$.  These are estimates for the
L132: integrands in the representation after taking the compensator, with earlier
L133: measurable factors kept inside the expectation.  They do not estimate the
L134: expected absolute value of an unprojected score.  The representations used
L135: for different lines or their improvements may be different; the table does
L136: not assert simultaneous bounds on one family of vectors.  The $L^2$ cost gains
L137: $n^{-0.004}$ for $l\ge2$ and $d\ge Tn^{-0.02}$, and the $L^1$ cost at order
L138: four gains $n^{-0.001}$ for $d\ge Tn^{-0.006}$.
L139: Stationary initialization contributes
L140: \[
L141:  \frac{1+u q_e(X_0)}{1+u \bar q_e}.
L142: \]
L143: We need a gain when these are the only differentiated factors.  If $p$ is
L144: a nonnegative stationary initial density with $\mu p=1$ and
L145: $\|p\|_\infty\le n^{C_0}$, then the exact replica identity is
L146: \begin{equation}\label{repl:initial-overlap}
L147:  \frac1{\binom n2}\sum_e \mu[pq_e]^2
L148:  =\frac{n\mu^{\otimes2}[p(X)p(X')\rho_2(X,X')^2]-1}{n-1}
L149:  \le C n^{4\beta}T^{-1}+n^{-A'}
L150: \end{equation}
L151: for every fixed $A'$.  Indeed choose the first dyadic $d_\circ\ge cT$, so
L152: $d_\circ\le2cT$, $r_2(d_\circ)\le c^{-1/2}r_2(T)$, and
L153: $a_2(d_\circ)\ge c_1 n^{3\beta}$.  This scale is among the query scales
L154: in Lemma~\ref{hist:static-support}.  Split at $|\rho_2|=r_2(d_\circ)$;
L155: the complementary probability is
L156: $\exp(-c n^{3\beta})$, which pays $\|p\|_\infty^2$.  This is the weighted
L157: replica identity used in the stationary comparison
L158: \cite[Section~8]{FUA}. %
L159: In particular
L160: \begin{equation}\label{repl:stationary-factor}
L161:  |\bar q|_2\lesssim_\beta T^{-1/2},\qquad
L162:  |\bar q|_4\lesssim_\beta T^{-1/4},\qquad |\bar q|_\infty\le1 .
L163: \end{equation}
L164: The normalized initial marginal of a tested stationary history is such a
L165: $p$: its density is at most $\|v_\alpha\|_\infty/z_\alpha$.  The coefficient
L166: of positive order $j$ in the initialization factor is
L167: $(-\bar q_e)^j+q_e(X_0)(-\bar q_e)^{j-1}$.  A numerator supplies at most one
L168: $q_e(X_0)$ on each history.  Thus if all positive orders come from
L169: initialization, at least one factor is either $\bar q$ or the integrated vector
L170: $\mu[pq_e]$; \eqref{repl:initial-overlap} and boundedness of the other
L171: factors give a fixed power saving.
L172: Suppose now a raw clock likelihood has a positive order.  Each path is a
L173: forest with $O(\log n)$ roots, or consists of the one or two complete legs.
L174: Chronologically earlier roots have lengths at least a constant times later
L175: ones.  Independent paths can be interleaved preserving this property:
L176: merge their lists in decreasing order of the greatest remaining root length,
L177: which is comparable to the current root length on each list.
L178: Project every differentiated root preceding the last such root onto its
L179: endpoints.  The conditional coefficient is
L180: \[
L181:  c_l^I=R_l(I)+q_e(X_{\sup I})R_{l-1}(I),
L182:  \qquad R_0=1,
L183: \]
L184: by \eqref{score:raw-conditional}.  This projection is within the expectation,
L185: using Lemma~\ref{hist:conditional-interior}; the endpoint factors of preceding
L186: roots are measurable before the last root.  After expanding their two
L187: monomials, all initialization coefficients can therefore be bounded by one
L188: in this calculation.
L189: If these preceding roots supply no positive-order $R$ factor, the last
L190: root, of order $l\le k$ and length $d\le CT$, uses the $L^1$ line of
L191: \eqref{repl:forward-costs}.  Its first term is $O(n^{-1/6})$.
L192: Since $T^{3/4}=\sqrt n$, its second term is at most
L193: $CT^{(l-4)/2}$ when $l\ge3$; when $l\le2$ it is at most $T^{-3/4}$,
L194: because $d\ge1$.  For $l<4$ there is a fixed power saving.  Put
L195: \[
L196:  \varepsilon_0=10^{-4}.
L197: \]
